record.context_brief: Unimodality of the secrecy ratio of a unimodular lattice
record.original_question: If L is a unimodular lattice, prove that its secrecy ratio r_L(y) = θ_(Z^n)(y) / θ_L(y) is unimodal for y ≥ 0 and attains its maximum at y = 1.

evidence.quote: The secrecy ratio of a lattice L is the ratio rL(y) = θZn (y) / θL(y), where the theta series is defined as θL(y) = Σx∈L qx.x, with q = exp(−πy).
Open Question 8.4. If L is a unimodular lattice prove that rL(y) is unimodal for y ≥ 0 with a maximum in y = 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a full-rank lattice $L\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, define its theta series by
\[ \theta_L(y) \;=\; \sum_{x\in L} q^{\,x\cdot x}, \qquad q = e^{-\pi y}, \quad y>0, \]
where $x\cdot x$ denotes the standard Euclidean inner product. For the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^n$, set $\theta_{\mathbb{Z}^n}(y)=\sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^n} q^{x\cdot x}$. A lattice $L\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is called unimodular if it equals its dual $L^*=\{v\in\mathbb{R}^n : v\cdot x\in\mathbb{Z}\ \forall x\in L\}$. For a unimodular lattice $L$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, define the secrecy ratio
\[ r_L(y) \;=\; \frac{\theta_{\mathbb{Z}^n}(y)}{\theta_L(y)}, \qquad y\geq 0. \]
Prove that for every unimodular lattice $L$, the function $y\mapsto r_L(y)$ is unimodal on $[0,\infty)$ and attains its maximum at $y=1$.
artifact.category_tag: Theta series of unimodular lattices (Belfiore–Solé conjecture)
artifact.status_search_result: This is the Belfiore–Solé secrecy-function conjecture. It has been verified for many specific families (e.g., all known extremal even unimodular lattices in dimensions less than 80, and unimodular lattices from Type II codes of length up to 40), but it remains open in general for unimodular lattices. Generalizations to $\ell$-modular and isodual/formally unimodular lattices have been disproved by explicit counterexamples, while the original unimodular case has neither been proved nor refuted.

status_evidence.title: On a conjecture by Belfiore and Solé on some lattices
status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture states the secrecy function of a unimodular lattice attains maximum at y=1; verified for several families.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture has been verified for specific families of unimodular lattices.

status_evidence.title: Counterexample to the l-modular Belfiore-Solé Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: For every l>1 there is a counterexample to the l-modular secrecy function conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The l-modular analogue of the conjecture is false, but the unimodular case is not addressed by these counterexamples.

status_evidence.title: On the Maximum Theta Series over Unimodular Lattices
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to investigate the maximum of theta-series ratios for unimodular lattices.
status_evidence.claim: The problem remains an active research topic for unimodular lattices.
